title: The North Wind Winds
notes: CORRECTION (2026-09-24): reassigned from sect_coast to sect_march. The earlier pass (2026-09-23) grounded this chapter in rgn_stepped_coast's terrace scar text and stopped there without checking every paralogue-tagged locations row -- the same class of error already caught once on ch_p_indech's note. A fuller pass found locations.loc_north_wind (region_id=rgn_drowned_march, 'the second hermit; likewise refuses') -- rgn_drowned_march's own direction column is literally 'north', and this chapter's own title is 'The North Wind Winds': name, direction, and the explicit 'second hermit' pairing with loc_hermit_lake (Indech, 'the first hermit', sect_coast) all point the same way. rgn_stepped_coast's terrace imagery was a real textual match but the wrong one -- npcs.npc_macuil never named a region itself, only 'refuses to adjudicate', which fits either hermit equally well and doesn't disambiguate. Regrounded in rgn_drowned_march's own scar ('a rift valley that filled; a lake with a visible former shoreline') and texture ('in dry years the top of a bell tower breaks the surface; villages sit on the new shoreline and farm the old one'); see maps.map_p_macuil's own note for the terrain rebuild. sect_march's own dual explanation_sacred/explanation_material columns reused for the same 'offers both, refuses to choose' device the old (wrong-region) version already had -- that narrative structure transfers cleanly, only the grounding under it changes.
teaches_system: a saint who will not judge

title: His Lake

CORRECTED (2026-09-23): the first pass checking for a sect_coast connection only read the regions tab (one row per claimed region) and missed the finer-grained locations/polities/settlements tabs. locations.loc_hermit_lake ('The saint's lake', region_id=rgn_stepped_coast, 'a hermit who refuses to adjudicate; fisher cult around him') is Indech's lake almost verbatim. polities.pol_isles (also rgn_stepped_coast) independently confirms it: 'a hermit saint lives here and refuses to adjudicate anything.' settlements.set_pelagos (also rgn_stepped_coast): 'fisher commune; the saint lives on the next island and they feed him' -- Pelagos IS the fisher cult. CORRECTION 2 (2026-09-24): the earlier note here also claimed Macuil was sect_coast's paralogue too, in this same region -- that was wrong (see ch_p_macuil's own corrected note). locations.loc_hermit_lake itself names Indech 'a hermit', and the paired loc_north_wind row (region_id=rgn_drowned_march) names Macuil 'the second hermit' in a DIFFERENT region -- sect_coast's own paralogue set is Indech and the Shadhavar (locations.loc_lowest_terrace, same region), not Indech and Macuil. teaches_system's shared 'a saint who will not judge' with ch_p_macuil is still deliberate parallel structure across two different sects, not evidence they share one.

title: The Lowest Terrace

This completes sect_coast's declared paralogue set (Indech + the Shadhavar, per every locations row tagged chapters='P' with region_id=rgn_stepped_coast); Macuil is not part of it, see that chapter's own corrected note. IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: the real pact/capture system (named's own addendum: 'three-way capture: intact / harvest / kill', 'the Named know each other: kill one and the next will not be captured') and the Shadhavar's own always-on song-pull mechanic are NOT implemented in map_grid.gd -- this chapter is built to the same skeleton depth as every other map this session (real terrain, a reachable objective, a scene), not a claim that the capture system itself now exists. ea_shadhavar (enemy_archetypes) represents it as a reachable/fightable stand-in the same way ea_warlord stands in for Macuil and Indech's own capstone fights.

title: The Mountain Above the Lake
notes: New (2026-09-24). sect_march's second declared paralogue, found the same way ch_p_shadhavar was: auditing every locations row tagged chapters='P'. locations.loc_simurgh_nest (region_id=rgn_drowned_march, 'The mountain above the lake', 'the Simurgh; a foster-mother who answers whoever holds the feather') and named.nmd_simurgh (same region -- pact_object='the feather', terms='answers whoever holds the feather, and answers anyone who holds it', signature_mechanic='5 HP/turn to rider and adjacent allies (flat, not percentage)', notes='cleanses corruption; the only thing that can strip a pact without a Pardoner, and will not do it on request'). Both independently point at rgn_drowned_march, already confirmed claimed_by_sect_id=sect_march via ch_p_macuil's own corrected note. This gives sect_march two declared paralogues (loc_north_wind/Macuil, loc_simurgh_nest/the Simurgh) against rgn_drowned_march's own locations rows -- no third one tagged chapters='P' exists for this region or rgn_the_shoulder (sect_march's other claimed region), so this completes sect_march's set the same way ch_p_shadhavar completed sect_coast's. SCOPE NOTE, same as every other named-creature paralogue this session: the real pact system (whoever holds the feather commands her, defects instantly on the feather changing hands, cleanses corruption 'will not do it on request') and the flat 5 HP/turn aura are NOT implemented in map_grid.gd -- this is a reachable/fightable skeleton encounter only, same honesty flag as ea_shadhavar's own row. The Simurgh reads as notably less adversarial than the Shadhavar or the Karkadann (nothing in named.nmd_simurgh suggests she attacks on sight) -- representing her as encounter_spawns kind='boss' is a bigger tonal stretch here than anywhere else this pattern has been used, flagged plainly rather than smoothed over.
teaches_system: help you cannot simply ask for

title: The Dove Colony
notes: New (2026-09-24). sect_vashti's first declared paralogue, found the same way ch_p_shadhavar/ch_p_simurgh were: auditing every locations row tagged chapters='P'. locations.loc_dove_colony (region_id=rgn_ashland, 'the Karkadann; it guards what it has decided to guard') and named.nmd_karkadann (same region -- pact_object='the nest it guards', terms='protects what it has decided to protect; nothing negotiates with it', defection_trigger='turns the moment you threaten the doves; state orders and its terms are simply incompatible', notes='the plain one on purpose -- the roster needs one straightforwardly good option'). rgn_ashland is already confirmed claimed_by_sect_id=sect_vashti (regions tab). locations.loc_cinder_track, an already-referenced Act2 location in this same region, independently calls its own ground 'the Karkadann's country' -- corroborating, not contradicting: cinder_track is the ash road THROUGH its territory, dove_colony is the guarded heart of it. rgn_ashland's other paralogue-tagged location, loc_buried_works ('records, complicit clerks, a shrine built over a facility'), is not a Named-creature site and is left for a separate paralogue. SCOPE NOTE, same as every other named-creature paralogue this session: the real pact system (guards only what it has decided to guard, turns hostile specifically if the doves are threatened, cannot be ordered) and its charge mechanic (strong vs mounted, stuck one turn after) are NOT implemented in map_grid.gd -- reachable/fightable skeleton only. Unlike the Shadhavar (eerie, uncontrolled) or the Simurgh (protective but withholding), named.nmd_karkadann's own notes call it 'the plain one on purpose... straightforwardly good' -- the least ambivalent of the Named encountered so far, closer to a hero-monster than a riddle. VALIDATOR NOTE (2026-09-24): canon_validate.py's c09 check now flags 3 consecutive 'seize' chapters on route='both'/column='unified' (ch_p_shadhavar, ch_p_simurgh, ch_p_karkadann). Reviewed, not fixed: all three genuinely have no stated objective in their own grounding text, and 'seize' is the same honest placeholder used for every paralogue map to date (map_p_macuil included) -- inventing artificial variety across them to quiet this warning would trade a real grounding gap for a fake one. Left as a known pacing gap for whenever paralogue objectives get real design attention.
teaches_system: a guardian whose terms are simple and absolute

title: The Interior of the Flats
notes: New (2026-09-24). sect_road's first declared paralogue, found the same way the last three were: auditing every locations row tagged chapters='P'. locations.loc_flats_interior (region_id=rgn_glass_flats, 'the Anzu; arrows come apart, and it reads what you cannot') and named.nmd_anzu (same region -- pact_object='the register itself', terms='contracts with whoever can READ the register, not who owns it', defection_trigger='someone demonstrates literacy you lack; ties to the hidden-literacy thread', signature_mechanic='contact degrades enemy weapons; only bites what is already worn; broken means unarmed, not dead'). rgn_glass_flats is already confirmed claimed_by_sect_id=sect_road (regions tab). loc_glass_edge, an existing Act2 location in the same region, corroborates rather than conflicts: it's the approach ('the edge of the Glass Flats'), this paralogue is the interior. objective_verb='seize' stays the honest placeholder, same reasoning already reviewed on ch_p_karkadann's own notes (nothing in either grounding source states a win condition) -- this is now a 4th consecutive placeholder-seize paralogue and c09 will likely flag it again; not fixed for the same reason: inventing variety not supported by the data would trade a real gap for a fake one. Notably sect_road already has a real, non-placeholder 'purchase' objective_verb precedent (ch_r16/map_b15, tied to the sect's own redemption-as-purchase doctrine) -- considered and rejected here, because named.nmd_anzu's own terms are explicitly about LITERACY, not currency ('contracts with whoever can READ the register, not who owns it') -- reusing 'purchase' would import the wrong mechanic just to avoid repetition. SCOPE NOTE, same as every other named-creature paralogue: the real pact/literacy-contract system and the weapon-degrading touch are NOT implemented in map_grid.gd -- reachable/fightable skeleton only.
teaches_system: a pact you must be able to read to keep

title: The Open Road
notes: New (2026-09-24). sect_road's second and final declared paralogue, found the same way ch_p_anzu was: auditing every locations row tagged chapters='P'. locations.loc_open_road (region_id=rgn_the_throat, 'The open road (no fixed site)', 'the Huma; it never lands, so it belongs to a road, not a place') and named.nmd_huma (same region -- pact_object='no seal; it cannot be owned', terms='cannot be owned, only flown under; its shadow legitimizes whoever it falls on', defection_trigger='never defects because it was never yours', signature_mechanic='MAP HAZARD, NOT A MOUNT: drifts overhead; marked units gain stats and become targeting priority for every enemy', notes='kill-taboo: whoever lands the blow dies in forty days, no reload undoes it'). rgn_the_throat is sect_road's own seat region, already confirmed claimed_by_sect_id=sect_road. With this, sect_road's declared paralogue set (rgn_glass_flats' loc_flats_interior + rgn_the_throat's loc_open_road) is complete. DESIGN DEPARTURE FROM THE OTHER FOUR NAMED PARALOGUES: this one explicitly is NOT a fightable capstone. named.nmd_huma's own text is unambiguous that it is a map hazard, not a mount, and that killing it carries a stated kill-taboo (death in forty days) rather than any reward -- giving it an encounter_spawns kind='boss' row the way the Shadhavar/Simurgh/Karkadann/Anzu all got would directly contradict its own grounding, not just stretch it the way ea_simurgh's did. So there is no ea_huma / no boss spawn here: the Huma appears only in this map's terrain/design_note text and the scene, drifting overhead as atmosphere, never as a targetable unit. objective_verb='escape' (not the usual placeholder 'seize') is the one real, grounded departure from every prior paralogue's objective: locations.loc_open_road is explicit 'no fixed site' -- there is nothing to seize -- and a road is crossed, not held. Reuses map_grid.gd's existing escape/escort win logic (min_solution_units units must reach the 'E' tile), same mechanism as map_a03. Ordinary road threats (reused ea_looter, same archetype already grounded for 'opportunists working the toll road' on sect_road's own map_r16) provide the actual combat, since a battle map needs contestable enemies and the Huma itself cannot be one.
teaches_system: a blessing that was never yours to keep

title: The Buried Works
notes: New (2026-09-24). sect_vashti's second and final declared paralogue, the last of all 8 locations rows tagged chapters='P' in canon.xlsx -- every sect's declared paralogue set is now built. locations.loc_buried_works ('The buried works, under Vashti', region_id=rgn_ashland, 'records, complicit clerks, a shrine built over a facility'). Unlike every other paralogue this session, this one has no named.* row -- rgn_ashland's only Named tie is nmd_karkadann, already spent on ch_p_karkadann/loc_dove_colony -- so there is no creature here at all, human antagonists only. Grounded directly in sects.sect_vashti's own wound ('collaboration: lords who hosted the experiments still hold office') and doctrine ('sacraments from complicit hands are void; the veneration must be re-made clean') -- the same 'complicit hands... re-made clean' refrain already used for map_v21's shrine-reconsecration defend map, and independently echoed a third time in calendar!C6 ('any calendar kept by complicit hands is void'). This paralogue is the literal version of that refrain: a shrine built OVER the buried facility where the experiments happened, its records still down there. Reuses ea_hardened_veteran for both the boss and mook spawn, same archetype and same justification ch_v21's own encounter_spawns row already used for 'the lord's household guard' -- 'complicit hands' generally, no named individual stated anywhere. objective_verb='seize' here is NOT the usual paralogue placeholder: every other paralogue's 'seize' was an honest default because nothing stated a win condition -- here the records themselves are explicitly the thing to reach, so 'seize the archive' is the directly grounded choice. CROSS-REFERENCE, not resolved here: ascension_signals.sig_unstained_respected ('whether the Unstained's refusal of him was honored or steamrolled in how their chapters/paralogue resolved') names 'their... paralogue' as one of its own inputs -- this is that paralogue. ascension_signals' own header note is explicit these signals are 'candidates, not a locked checklist' and belong to their own authored-decision session -- noted here as a real connection, not wired into any flag or GameState mechanic.
teaches_system: what a shrine is built to bury
